root_cause.text: Missing resource cleanup in the error path of snd_cx88_hw_params() allows DMA mapping resources allocated by cx88_alsa_dma_map() to leak when cx88_risc_databuffer() fails.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds cx88_alsa_dma_unmap(chip) call in the error handling block after cx88_risc_databuffer() returns a negative value. The function cx88_alsa_dma_map() is called earlier in the function to acquire DMA resources, but when cx88_risc_databuffer() fails, the code jumps to the error label without releasing these resources. The fix ensures that cx88_alsa_dma_unmap() is invoked to properly release the DMA mapping before exiting on error, preventing resource leaks in the cx88 ALSA audio driver.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function contains a resource leak in the error path. At line 408, videobuf_pci_dma_map() is called to map DMA resources. If this succeeds but the subsequent cx88_risc_databuffer() call at line 412-413 fails, the error handler at line 429-431 only calls kfree(buf) without unmapping the DMA resources allocated by videobuf_pci_dma_map(). The DMA mapping created at line 408 is never cleaned up when the error occurs at line 414-415, causing a resource leak. The fix would require calling videobuf_pci_dma_unmap() or similar cleanup before kfree(buf) in the error path.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces a resource leak in snd_cx88_hw_params(). The function calls cx88_alsa_dma_init() at line 488-489, then cx88_alsa_dma_map() at line 491-492. If cx88_risc_databuffer() fails at line 495-496, the error path at line 497 'goto error' does not properly clean up the DMA mapping resources. The error label (not shown in diff but implied) would need to call cx88_alsa_dma_unmap() before cx88_alsa_dma_free(), but the diff shows no such cleanup in the error path. The old code using videobuf_dma_unmap() and videobuf_dma_free() was replaced with cx88_alsa_dma_unmap() and cx88_alsa_dma_free(), but the error handling in snd_cx88_hw_params() was not updated to call cx88_alsa_dma_unmap() when cx88_risc_databuffer() fails. This leaves the DMA mapping (allocated by dma_map_sg in cx88_alsa_dma_map) unmapped, causing a resource leak.
